correctness.rationale: The polynomial follows by whether neither, u, or v is chosen: (1+z)^(a+b)+z((1+z)^a+(1+z)^b). With Re z=x>=0, s=|1+z|>r=|z|, s>=1, and s²-2r=(r-1)²+2x>=0. For a=min(a,b)=0, |(1+z)^(b+1)|>r. For a=1, factor (1+z)[(1+2z)(1+z)^(b-1)+z]; the first factor nonzero and |1+2z|²-r²=1+4x+3r²>0. For a>=2, root would imply s^a<=r(1+s^(a-b))<=2r<=s²<=s^a. At s>1 this is impossible for a<b or a=b>2; when a=b=2, all equalities imply x=0,r=1, z=±i, at which (1+z)²+2z=±4i ≠0. The edge K2, star, singleton boundaries hold. Independently constructed independence polynomials for all 0<=a,b<=8 and numerically evaluated all roots, with max tested real part approx -0.144056 at (8,8); only analytic moduli proof is unrestricted.

originality.rationale: Brown–Cameron establish stars, low independence number, and nonstable trees; Zhang–Tu extend to spiders with one branching center; neither result covers proper double-stars with two branching vertices and arbitrarily many leaves. Hibi–Kara–Vien Proposition 3.1 already implies the displayed polynomial enumeration identity, which is not claimed new, while Bencs yields a special real-rooted D2,2 subfamily, not arbitrary unequal a,b. The new assertion is strict left-half-plane zero exclusion for the entire double-star family. Full text Zhang–Tu was inaccessible and Oxford VPN disconnected; its precise theorem from metadata describes spiders; overlap remains residual.
